assessmentHint.title: Alaska Wildfires and Sea Ice (example entrance/exit ticket)

answers.title: 1. What do you notice about the relationship between wildfires in Alaska and sea ice coverage?
answers.value: When sea ice melts there is less white surface to reflect sunlight, so more heat stays in the ocean and land.

answers.title: 2. Use cause and effect to explain how changes in one system might affect the other.
answers.value: Less sea ice means more open water absorbs heat, which can dry out forests and make wildfires more likely in Alaska.

answers.title: 1. What do you notice about the relationship between wildfires in Alaska and sea ice coverage?
answers.value: The graphs show sea ice going down over time while wildfire activity goes up in some years.

answers.title: 2. Use cause and effect to explain how changes in one system might affect the other.
answers.value: When sea ice decreases, then more heat is absorbed by the ocean, which can raise temperatures on land and cause more wildfires.

answers.title: 1. What do you notice about the relationship between wildfires in Alaska and sea ice coverage?
answers.value: Sea ice and wildfires both changed a lot after 2000 on the graph.

answers.title: 2. Use cause and effect to explain how changes in one system might affect the other.
answers.value: If the Arctic warms because there is less sea ice, then plants and soil dry out faster, which can lead to bigger wildfires.
